newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Suspected rebels torch five buses in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Suspected rebels torch five buses in Colombia.

text.p: Suspected leftist guerrillas hijacked and burned five buses, including one transporting boy scouts, on a highway in northwest Colombia early on Sunday, police said. No injuries were reported.

The latest incident, which took place near the town of Yarumal on the route between the city of Medellin and the coast, raises to 38 the number of vehicles destroyed by guerrillas in the province in the last week, a police spokesman said.
Regional army commander Gen. Carlos Ospina offered "substantial rewards" for information about those responsible for the wave of attacks.
Provincial governor Alvaro Uribe said, meanwhile, he would be setting up an "intelligence network" along the province's major highways to forewarn of possible guerrilla attacks on traffic.

Both the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the country's largest guerrilla force, and the National Liberation Army (ELN), founded by radical Roman Catholic priests in the mid-1960s, set up roadblocks on major highways and torch vehicles that try to defy the order to stop. The tactic appears to be aimed at disrupting both passenger and cargo transport.
